assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a discovery chain from hormone biology to drugs that transformed diabetes and obesity care, with large effects on cardiovascular and metabolic outcomes. The impact on medicine and on the physiology of gut-pancreas-brain signalling is clear and still expanding.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, proglucagon processing, translation to therapy) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide form) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's contribution is largely industrial drug design (liraglutide, semaglutide) and the list has four names, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in many independent trials and clinical practice over nearly two decades; interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among early peptide identification, physiology and drug development; the three-person limit forces exclusion of Knudsen.
Detailed priority claims are recalled from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with population-level evidence of strong reductions in precancer in vaccinated cohorts. This is a rare case of basic virology and cell biology giving cancer prevention.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach at NCI; Frazer contributed early VLP expression and vaccine development. Parallel work by others and the death of Jian Zhou complicate credit; the supplied names support a coherent three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: licensed for roughly two decades, with cohort and registry data showing reductions in CIN and invasive cervical cancer. Timing is appropriate since cancer outcome data are now strong.
uncertainties: Priority among several groups, including contributors not on the list.
Whether the committee sees the discovery as sufficiently distinct from the earlier recognition of HPV as a cause of cervical cancer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling, with IRE1 as the sensor, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and downstream transcriptional control. It is conceptually original, shaped understanding of proteostasis, and is linked to diabetes, cancer, neurodegeneration and secretory disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter (IRE1 and the mechanism of the response, unconventional splicing) and Mori (UPR elements and the transcriptional response in yeast and mammals) are the clearest pair; the list supports exactly these two.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed by decades of independent work and is textbook. Clinical translation is still developing, but the criterion concerns the discovery itself, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with contributors not on the list.
Therapeutic relevance remains less established than the basic importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids opened a new experimental system for tissue biology, disease modelling and personalised medicine, building on Lgr5 stem cell identification. Methodological and conceptual influence across fields is wide.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader (Lgr5 stem cell identity, the culture system); Sato was the lead experimentalist on the intestinal organoid papers. Both credited names support a pair, and recognition of Clevers alone is also conceivable.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and adopted; clinical impact is still emerging, which weakens maturity somewhat, but the technique is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is still limited and may yet grow.
Relation to earlier 3D culture and stem-cell work whose credit is not on the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death rather than only increased proliferation, and defined the apoptosis regulatory network. Venetoclax-type BH3 mimetic therapy gives strong clinical confirmation of a mechanism-based discovery.
assessment.attribution: Adams and Cory (BCL-2 gene characterisation and the protein family) and Vaux (survival function of BCL-2 in cells) are a reasonable trio; Strasser's contributions are important but later. Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize and with other contributors not on the list makes credit sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Mature: mechanism confirmed by structure, genetics and clinical trials, with approved drugs.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the work as sufficiently distinct from earlier apoptosis recognition.
Key contributors absent from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living cell therapy. The concept, costimulatory design and clinical proof are of high impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation and preclinical proof), June (clinical translation in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials) can form a reasonable prize, although other founding contributors are not on the list and any trio leaves someone out.
assessment.maturity: Clinically confirmed in several indications, but toxicity, durability and success in solid tumours remain open. Recognition may be early for the field as a whole but strong for B-cell malignancies.
uncertainties: Compound discovery whose conceptual and clinical parts may need different recognition.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and long-term safety data still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib turned CML from a fatal into a chronic disease and established the paradigm of targeting an oncogenic kinase. It is one of the clearest examples of molecularly targeted therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (drug discovery), Druker (clinical development and evidence) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and follow-on drugs) are a natural trio. Credit for BCR-ABL genetics sits with others not listed.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with more than two decades of survival data. Recognition might be viewed as primarily drug development rather than mechanism discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as drug development rather than discovery of mechanism.
Distribution of credit between industrial and academic contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR defined a central nutrient-sensing regulator of cell growth, metabolism and ageing, with implications for cancer, immunosuppression and metabolic disease. Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin changed how growth control is understood.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified the TOR genes and their function in yeast; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin was an important step toward the target. Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work is highly relevant, but attribution is unresolved, so I prefer the two-name configuration; other contributors not on the list add uncertainty.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across species and in disease; clinical use of rapalogs is established, though the broader mechanistic picture is still evolving.
uncertainties: Attribution among Hall, rapamycin pharmacology and mammalian mTOR work is unresolved.
Details recalled from memory, not independently verified.
